questions.stem: A pool has 4 crews. In week 7, three jobs needing 2, 1 and 1 crews are under way, and a job needing 1 crew is a candidate to start that week. Which test does add_cumulative(intervals, demands, 4) apply to week 7?

options.text: Demands running: 4 before the candidate, within 4, so the job may start
options.says: The candidate's own demand counts too: once it starts it runs in week 7, so the sum is 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 5.

options.text: Largest demand running: 2, within 4, so the job may start
options.says: Every running interval's demand counts, summed; the largest one alone is not the test.

options.text: Jobs running: 4 with the candidate, not below 4, so the job may not start
options.says: The constraint counts demands, not jobs, and allows a total equal to the capacity: the test is sum of demands <= capacity.

options.text: Demands running: 5 with the candidate, above 4, so the job may not start
options.says: Right: in each week the demands of the intervals running then are added and compared with the capacity.

origin.section: Cumulative Caps the Crews at Work in Every Week

questions.stem: A pool has 5 crews all season except weeks 10 to 13, when only 3 are available. How do you state that with a single add_cumulative call?

options.text: Capacity 5, and a fixed interval on weeks 10 to 13 with demand 2
options.says: Right: the capacity is the peak, and the fixed interval holds the 5 - 3 = 2 crews that are away.

options.text: Capacity 3, and no fixed interval anywhere in the season
options.says: That wastes 2 crews in every other week; the lesson keeps the capacity at the peak and holds the gap only where it occurs.

options.text: Capacity 5, and a fixed interval on weeks 10 to 13 with demand 3
options.says: The fixed interval's demand is the crews missing, peak - available = 2; demand 3 leaves only 2 crews for the work.

options.text: Capacity 3, and a fixed interval on weeks 10 to 13 with demand 2
options.says: With capacity 3 the season never has 5 crews, and the fixed interval leaves 1 crew in weeks 10 to 13.

origin.section: A Capacity That Drops Is a Fixed Interval Holding the Missing Crews

questions.stem: A 3-week clear must lie wholly inside one of its region's outage windows, [4, 9) or [15, 20), in weeks. Which domain should its start variable get?

options.says: These are the windows, not the starts: a start at week 8 would run the job to week 10, past the window. A start ranges up to b - d.
Right: starts a to b - d, ends included: 9 - 3 = 6 and 20 - 3 = 17.
from_intervals includes both ends, so the last start is b - d, not b - d - 1; a start at 6 ends at 9, the window's end.
A start before the window's first week puts the job's first weeks outside the outage.

origin.section: An Outage Window Is a Domain on the Start
